letters.shape_note: A small open hook at the lower left that swings into one smooth bowl. The bowl's right side runs up into the tick. Most consonants wear this tick; a vowel sign usually takes its place.
A small closed loop low on the left, then a cup whose right side rises as a free arm. The tick sits over the left part.
The long 'ā' sign. The tick on top is replaced by a bar that runs out to the right and ends in a small ring hanging from it.
The short vowel 'a' written by itself, as at the start of a word. No tick.
The simplest consonant: a plain circle-like bowl with the tick on top.

example.en: come (to a close friend or a child)

letters.shape_note: The long vowel 'ā' by itself. It is అ with the right side pinched in at the middle: the top-right curl closes into a ring with a short tail, and the bowl ends under it.
A circle as tall as the letter's body, written after the letter. It adds an 'm' or 'n' sound after the vowel; at the end of a word it sounds like 'm'.
Under the tick, a rounded top bends back through a flat middle bar into a bottom bowl that opens to the left, a little like a rounded 5. It has no closed loop.
A small closed loop at the lower left, then a bowl whose right side runs up into the tick, so the top is closed. The sound is between English 'v' and 'w'.
The short 'i' sign. The tick is replaced by a small closed curl on top of the letter.
The short vowel 'i' by itself.
A wide open curve with a small ring inside at the left. It has no tick.
The long 'ī' sign. Like the short 'i' curl on top, but the curl carries on into a second small twist.
The long vowel 'ī' by itself. Not built from ఇ: learn it as its own shape.
Like అ with a tick on top: a wide bowl with a small ring inside at the left. Where అ has a flat bar on the right, త has a second small ring. The tongue touches the teeth.
A rounded body with a short notch rising from the middle of the bottom, with the tick on top. The tongue touches the teeth.
The short 'u' sign: a hook added on the right side of the letter. The tick on top stays.
The short vowel 'u' by itself.
Like వ, but open at the top: the body does not close under the tick.
The long 'ū' sign: the short 'u' hook on the right, plus a bar that runs on to the right and ends in a small hanging ring, like the 'ā' sign.
The long vowel 'ū' by itself. It is ఉ with a second upright stroke on top and an extra curl on the right.
Doubled 'm', held a little longer. The second మ changes shape: at the lower right it is a round curl with a small ring inside.
Doubled 'n'. The second న hangs at the lower right without its tick, and its long arm sweeps up the right side of the first.
Doubled 'k'. The second క changes shape: at the lower right it is a tall hook with a flat bar on top.
Doubled 'l'. The second ల changes shape: underneath it is a small arch with two humps.
Doubled 'v', as in నువ్వు, the close-friend 'you'. The second వ hangs at the lower right, nearly full size and without its tick; its long arm sweeps up the right side of the first and ends in a hook.
An arch open at the bottom, with the tick on top.
Like ద, but the left side starts with a flat bar sticking out to the left, and the body stays open above that bar. The tick is on top.
The short 'e' sign. The tick is replaced by a flat bar on top that sticks out to the left.
The short vowel 'e' by itself.

A 'd' made with the tongue curled back. Like ద on the left and along the bottom, but the right side differs: the top stroke ends in a free tip at the upper right instead of coming down, and the bottom right curls into a small closed loop.
The long 'ē' sign. Like the short 'e' stroke on top, with an extra upward tail.
The long vowel 'ē' by itself. It is ఎ with one extra stroke on top.
Doubled 't'. The second త changes shape: underneath it is a flat line that curls into one loop at the right, not a small త.
Doubled 'p'. The second ప hangs at the lower right without its tick, and its long arm sweeps up the right side of the first.
Doubled 'd'. The second ద is written small underneath, without its tick.
Doubled 'ch'. The second చ hangs at the lower right without its tick, and its long arm sweeps up the right side of the first.
Like న, but the right side does not join the tick: it ends in a free tip, leaving a gap under the tick.
Wider than మ. మ has a small loop low on the left; య has a big round ring there.
The short 'o' sign. The tick is replaced by a curl on top that swings over to the right and ends in a small ring.
The short vowel 'o' by itself.
A 't' made with the tongue curled back. An open cup with no tick. A short upright stroke stands on a ring at its top left.
The long 'ō' sign. Like the short 'o' curl on top, with an extra upward tail.
The long vowel 'ō' by itself. It is ఒ with one extra stroke on top.
Doubled 'y'. The second య is not written underneath: it becomes a long tail on the right. You will see the same tail in అన్నయ్య, the usual way to call an older brother.
It has no tick. The left side starts with a small curl at the top, and the bottom has a short notch in the middle. There is no closed loop.
Close to బ, but the top-left curl runs on to the right and ends in a second hook at the top right, and the right arm stays short beneath that hook. It has no tick.
The 'ai' sign has two parts: the 'e' stroke on top and a second mark under the letter, a loop with a flat line running right.
The vowel 'ai' by itself (as in English 'my').
An 'l' made with the tongue curled back. It has a tick on top.
An 'n' made with the tongue curled back. A wide letter with no tick.
The 'au' sign. It replaces the tick with the 'e' bar sticking out to the left, which runs on to the right and ends in a small hanging ring.
The vowel 'au' by itself (as in English 'now').

example.en: yes (a less common spelling of అవును)

letters.shape_note: A body with a small loop at the lower left, with the tick on top. What marks it out: a bar running out to the right from the top, ending in a small ring.
A soft 'sh'. It has a tick on top.
A 'sh' made with the tongue curled back. It is ప with one extra stroke that crosses the lower right corner and hangs below with a hook.
This mark removes the 'a' that a plain consonant carries: the consonant is said with no vowel after it. On a letter with a tick it takes the tick's place. Seen mostly at the end of borrowed words.
A consonant followed by 'r'. The ర turns into a wide cup drawn under the whole letter. It does not look like ర.
స with the under-form of క at its lower right, the same hook with a flat bar as in క్క.
Doubled ట. The second one is written small underneath, without its upright stroke.
స with the under-form of త beneath it, the same flat line and loop as in త్త.
Doubled 's'. The second స hangs at the lower right as a smaller స without its tick, and its long arm sweeps up the right side of the first.
ష with a small ట underneath, without its upright stroke.
'k' with a puff of air. Its own shape, not built from క. It has no tick, and a small stroke underneath like most of the other breathy letters.
'g' with a puff of air. It has a small stroke underneath, the usual sign of a breathy letter.
't' with a puff of air (never the English 'th'). A round body with a dot in the middle and a small stroke underneath.
'd' with a puff of air. It is ద with a small stroke underneath. థ has the same stroke and a dot in the middle as well.
'ch' with a puff of air. It is చ with a small stroke underneath.
'j' with a puff of air. A rare letter: learn to recognise it.
A consonant followed by 'y'. The య becomes the same long tail on the right as in య్య.
A consonant followed by 'v'. The వ hangs at the lower right without its tick; its long arm sweeps up the right side of the first letter and ends in a hook.
Doubled ళ. The second ళ hangs at the lower right without its tick, and its long arm sweeps up the right side of the first.
Doubled 'g'. The second గ is written small underneath, without its tick.
Doubled డ. The second one is written small underneath, without its tick.
Doubled 'b'. The second బ hangs at the lower right, and its long arm sweeps up the right side of the first.
'p' with a puff of air; in borrowed words it is said as 'f'. It is ప with a small stroke underneath.
'b' with a puff of air. It is బ with a tick on top and a small stroke underneath.
ట with a puff of air. It is ర with a dot in the middle.
డ with a puff of air. It is డ with a small stroke underneath.
An old second letter for 'r'. Modern writing uses ర instead: learn only to recognise it.
Doubled 'j'. The second జ is written small underneath.
ర with a small థ underneath: 'r' followed by a breathy 't'.
A sign found in Sanskrit words, said 'ru' in everyday speech. A large hook that drops from the right side well below the letter and curls back; the tick stays.
A vowel found in a few Sanskrit words, said 'ru'.
Two small circles, one above the other, after the letter: a light 'h' after the vowel. Rare, in Sanskrit words.
'k' and 'sh' together. It is written as one special shape: learn it whole.
The 'ng' sound of 'sing'. Almost never written by itself: recognise it only.
The 'ny' sound of 'canyon'. Seen almost only inside జ్ఞ.
జ with a small ఞ underneath. In everyday speech it is said 'gny' or 'gy', not 'jny'.
క with a smaller స hanging at the lower right, its long arm sweeping up the right side of క. It turns up in English loans: 'taxi', 'box', 'thanks'. Don't mix it up with క్ష, which has its own shape.
